name: CrossLoop
summary: Turns a public web page into a narrated launch video in three formats (16:9, 9:16, 4:5) with captions and suggested social copy, sold as one-time credit packs instead of a subscription.
best_for: founders and small SaaS, AI-tool and ecommerce teams who need a narrated launch or promo video for a product page or a Product Hunt or LinkedIn launch, without hiring an editor or paying for a monthly video subscription
skip_if: you need full control over the script and edit, talking-head avatars or long training videos, or you make videos every week and already pay for an editor or a video tool
honest_knock: The money-back guarantee covers only your first purchase, and films are deleted after 30 days, so anything you do not download is gone. The pages we read do not describe editing or revisions: the film is made from what your page says, so a thin page gives a thin film. CrossLoop is run by one named person, Harsha Vardhan, according to the terms, which is worth knowing if you plan to rely on it for a long time.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Launch Film · per one-time, one-time credit packs, no subscription: Launch Film $9 (1 credit), Launch Film Studio $19 (2 credits), Studio Pack 5 films $49 (10 credits), Studio Pack 20 films $129 (40 credits)
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-24 on crossloop.ai/pricing, crossloop.ai/terms and crossloop.ai/refund-policy, both last updated 10 October 2026) No subscription: you buy one-time credit packs. Launch Film is $9 for 1 credit, Launch Film Studio $19 for 2 credits (adds Trend Pulse, a script written around this week's news and TikTok trends in your niche), Studio Pack: 5 films $49 for 10 credits and Studio Pack: 20 films $129 for 40 credits, unless a different price is shown at checkout. A Launch film uses 1 credit and a Studio film 2. Narration in your own voice is +$9 a film after recording about 30 seconds once (Launch + your voice $18, Studio + your voice $28). Credits never expire. Each film comes in 16:9, 9:16 and 4:5 with a 30-second Instagram Reel and cover, a captions file (.srt) and LinkedIn and Instagram copy; nine languages are included. There is a 7-day money-back guarantee on the first purchase only, and a failed render returns the credit automatically. Payments run through Lemon Squeezy as merchant of record.

compare_with.name: InVideo
compare_with.why: InVideo is in our dossiers: Starter at $20 per seat a month with 400 credits per seat, read on 24 September 2026, and it turns a prompt or script into a first-draft video you edit yourself. CrossLoop starts from your web page instead of a prompt, costs $9 or $19 per film with no subscription, and hands back a finished film in three formats. InVideo fits a team that makes video every month and wants to edit; CrossLoop fits an occasional launch video.

exit_test.what: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. On 13 November 2026 the session tested CrossLoop with 2 film credits: one launch film generated from a site URL, and an attempt to set the script by description. Nothing was downloaded, posted or shared. Group 1: the URL https://aibuildermarketplace.com/ was used with Launch Film, English and Match my brand, started at about 17:20 after the first attempts described below. The status moved from Queued 4% to Reading your site 15%, Rendering videos 80% and Ready, after about 16 minutes. Credits went from 2 to 1. The result page says Your film is ready, 61 seconds, 1920x1080. The downloads are Reel 9:16 (30 seconds, with captions clear of the buttons of the app), 16:9 Landscape, 9:16 Story cut, 4:5 Portrait and Captions as an .srt file. The share link lasts 7 or 30 days. Ready made texts for LinkedIn and Instagram with hashtags are included. The film uses images from the tested site itself: at 0:20 a screen headed 01, Problem first, What do you need to solve? shows plan cards for Apollo at 49 dollars per seat, AISDR at 1.50 dollars, ActiveCampaign at 49 dollars a month and LocalTry at 59 dollars. The texts mention 659 tools, dated prices, who should skip it and Price Watch with 595 pages, all read from the site. Nothing was downloaded or posted. Group 2: the description For small business buyers. Calm and clear. End with this exact line: Every review shows the date we checked the price. gave, after Make my film, the error that the direction could not be checked, try again in a minute or leave it empty. A second try after about 1 minute gave the same error. Only with the field empty did the film go into production. No script editor or revision button was seen on the result page. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: A description with an exact closing line was refused twice with an error, and only an empty description started the film. The film language defaulted to Dutch from the browser. No script editor was seen.

sessions.what: We made one launch film in CrossLoop on 13 November 2026 from our own homepage address, using one of the two credits the account started with. The account is Daan's, and our AI assistant did the clicking. We downloaded, posted and shared nothing. We did not open Buy credits, so checkout, support and cancellation were not tested.
findings: The dashboard offers a Launch Film at $9 for 1 credit and a Launch Film Studio at $19 for 2 credits. It asks for a page address and a film style, and has an optional box of 400 characters to describe the film. The account started with 2 credits and no card was asked for.

We pasted our homepage address and chose Launch Film in English with the Match my brand style. The status moved from Queued to Reading your site to Rendering videos, and the film was ready after about 16 minutes. The vendor says about 15. Credits went from 2 to 1.

The result was a 61-second narrated film, offered as a 16:9 landscape cut, a 9:16 reel and story cut, a 4:5 portrait cut and a captions file, plus ready-made post text for LinkedIn and Instagram. The pictures and numbers in the film came from our own site. Films are kept for 30 days.

We then asked for a fixed closing line in the description box: 'End with this exact line: Every review shows the date we checked the price.' The form refused it twice with 'We couldn't check your direction right now.' The film only started with the box left empty. We found no script editor or revision button on the result page, so a fixed line could not be tested.
